messages:
elaine: Ok team, we need a small, canonical span naming + attribute surface for every LLM API request that we emit. Current dashboards and SLOs are noisy because everyone names spans differently.

devon: +1. Quick clarification: are we standardizing the root RPC span only, and leaving model internals as optional child spans?

elaine: Exactly. Root span = one per external API call. Keep span.name low-cardinality (suggestion: `llm.request`) and put route/model/etc in attributes. Child spans for cache checks, KV ops, generation steps are optional and can be sampled.

sudhir: low-cardinal names are critical. If we let route strings flow into span.name we blow up aggregation. Use `llm.request` and attributes for differentiation.

kevin: Proposed minimal attribute set (first draft):
```
span.name = "llm.request"\nservice.name = "redwood-inference"\nredwood.api_bucket = "api|stream|embed|rerank"  # coarse route bucket\nllm.model.name = "meta-llama-2-70b"\nllm.model.revision = "v2.1"\nllm.model.variant = "q4_0"\nllm.tokens.prompt = 42\nllm.tokens.generated = 128\nllm.kv_cache = "miss"|"partial"|"hit"\nllm.kv_cache_size = "small|medium|large"\nllm.batch_size = 8\nllm.routing_policy = "cost|latency|tiered"\ntelemetry.retention = "root_90d_children_7d_sampled_1pct_365d"\ntelemetry.sampling_reason = "error_rate_based|manual|probabilistic"\n```

sam: token counts are fine from a privacy POV as long as we don't log raw prompt text. rounding/integers OK. Also prefer buckets for cache size rather than exact numbers to keep cardinality low.

devon: Question: what about `http.route`? Customers create tons of custom routes; it will explode cardinality. Maybe only include `http.route` when a workspace opts in? Or transform to `redwood.route_bucket`.

elaine: Agreed. Default is to omit exact `http.route` and emit `redwood.api_bucket`. Per-workspace config can enable `http.route` but exporters must redact before leaving our trust boundary.

kevin: Exporter action items: redact any workspace-specific route strings, enforce model-name canonicalization, and attach the retention tag at ingest. Hashing routes was proposed but makes queries harder; coarse buckets are better.

sudhir: On model names: we must canonicalize and whitelist acceptable patterns before emitting. Strip path components, only allow [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Reject or map others to `unknown` to avoid leakage of internal identifiers.

sam: Sampling/retention strategy proposal: keep all root-span attributes for 90 days, keep child spans (detailed internals) for 7 days by default, and sample 1% of full traces for long-term storage (365d). Emit `telemetry.retention` attribute to indicate policy used.

devon: tiny nit: OTEL conventions often use `llm.tokens.*` rather than `llm.request.tokens.*`. Should we align with OTEL by using `llm.tokens.prompt` & `llm.tokens.generated`?

elaine: Good call. Let's standardize on `llm.tokens.*`. Update PRs accordingly.

kevin: Also recommend `llm.kv_cache` enumerate values instead of boolean `kv_cache_hit` to capture partial hits without adding cardinality.

sudhir: For `llm.kv_cache_size`, use approximate buckets (small/medium/large) and document the thresholds. Keep attr values consistent across SDKs.

sam: Docs + alerts: we need examples of queries for common alerts (e.g., spike in generated tokens per request, rise in kv partial hits) and how retention affects debug flows.

elaine: Actions:
- sudhir: implement canonicalizer in tracer to clean model names and apply route bucketing (WIP) 
- kevin: exporter changes to redact route, surface `telemetry.retention`, and default retention enforcement
- devon: author final attribute schema + per-workspace opt-in knobs for `http.route` and sampling
- sam: publish telemetry docs + alert playbook referencing these attributes
otel-bot: RFC updated: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/llm-span-attrs (comments open until EOD Friday)

devon: I'm happy with `span.name = llm.request` + the attribute list. If no objections I'll open the unified-spec PR tomorrow.

kevin: thumbs up. will start SDK tracer updates after spec lands.

elaine: thanks everyone. keeping this minimal and configurable is the goal. :rocket:
